# Research

::: lead
My research focuses on active travel, cycling, spatial data, and inequalities in mobility. I am particularly interested in how the built environment shapes travel behaviour and how data can help us better understand transport systems.
:::

## Current research

### [ATRAPA](https://webs.uab.cat/atrapa/)

*The Active Travel Backlash Paradox*

Research on the public acceptability of sustainable active-travel interventions and their social, political, and spatial implications.

- Validating OpenStreetMap for detecting cycling-infrastructure change (Barcelona, 2015–2023) *(paper in preparation, WP1)*

### [Active commuting to school among Spanish adolescents](https://github.com/eugenividal/acs_inequalities)

Research on social inequalities, neighbourhood context, and active commuting to and from school.

### [spanishoddata](https://github.com/rOpenSpain/spanishoddata)

Contribution to an R package for accessing and analysing large Spanish mobility datasets. 

## Previous postdoctoral research

### [SATURN](https://github.com/saturnlighting)

Supporting Active Travel Using Road-lighting at Night.

### [CRUSE](https://www.cruse.bike/)

Cycle Route Uptake & Scenario Estimation tool for Transport Infrastructure Ireland.

## PhD research

My PhD thesis, *Cycling and Socioeconomic Disadvantage*, examined inequalities in cycling participation, infrastructure access, travel behaviour, and safety.

- [Cycling and socioeconomic (dis)advantage](https://doi.org/10.1016/bs.atpp.2022.04.009)
- [Cycling behaviour and socioeconomic disadvantage](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tra.2021.08.004)
- [Infrastructure is not enough](https://doi.org/10.5198/jtlu.2021.1781)
- [Socioeconomic inequalities in cycling safety](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jth.2021.101291)

## Early research

During my MSc studies, I developed several projects on active travel, cycling, spatial analysis, and inequalities.

- [Inequalities in active travel in England](docs/Dissertation.pdf)
